passages.title: A staging question
passages.text: The retained RSC teaching account asks about setting, aims, relationships and positioning in a specific play. Such prompts do not establish what every gesture means or what an audience perceived.

passages.title: Original words and proposed timing
passages.text: At 2 s, A: Is this for me? At 6 s, B: I left it here. At 10 s, A: Then I’ll wait. Setup at 0 s; proposed end at 14 s. An unmarked envelope remains at (0,0). These are targets, not measured event times.
passages.context: Original fictional scenario; associated source supplies a method/context only, not these facts.

passages.title: Original score: facing
passages.text: Dimensionless plan: audience reference (0,-3); +x points right, +y away from the audience. A is at (-1,0), orientation 0° (+x). B is at (1,0), orientation 180° (-x). No movement is prescribed during the scored interval.
passages.context: Original fictional scenario; associated source supplies a method/context only, not these facts.

passages.title: Original score: offset
passages.text: Use the same words, timing targets and envelope. A is at (-1,1), orientation 270° (-y). B remains at (1,0), orientation 270° (-y). Orientation is a plan reference, not required eye contact or a personality trait.
passages.context: Original fictional scenario; associated source supplies a method/context only, not these facts.

claims.text: Identify all three planned spatial changes.
claims.qualification: Original unperformed scene and dimensionless score analysis. No actor, audience report, controlled causal effect or universal gesture meaning is supplied.

context: The original preparation contains the complete coordinates, events and two maps. Its observation records remain unfilled.
The RSC refresh timeout and caption inconsistency remain retained limitations. No source scene, photograph, critic quotation or recording is copied.
reviewLimitations: Local author check only. No independent reviewer, professional credential, actual learner/access observation, community endorsement or physical outcome is claimed.

lenses.label: Count the changed factors
lenses.observation: A’s position and both orientations change; B’s position stays fixed.
lenses.question: Why is this not a single-variable causal experiment?
readings: Three planned spatial factors change, even before any real performance occurs.
Actual timing, delivery, access mode, viewpoint and order could vary too.
lenses.boundary: An authored control is not a measured constancy.

lenses.label: Mark a prediction as a prediction
lenses.observation: No actual performance or observer record accompanies the scores.
lenses.question: What might you notice first, and what supports that prediction?
readings: Locate a specific position or timing feature, and permit an unknown response.
Offer an alternative interpretation compatible with the same score.
lenses.boundary: Do not convert predicted attention or emotion to an audience result.

lenses.label: Separate reports from events
lenses.observation: A future comparison would need dated event descriptions and situated reports.
lenses.question: How would you relate an interpretation to an observable feature?
readings: Record the event locator, deviations, observer viewpoint and access mode.
Keep performer intention, event description and observer interpretation in separate fields.
lenses.boundary: No imitation, acting, recording or participant recruitment is required here.

activity.transfer: Write one prediction, one possible contrary report and the event evidence needed to compare them. Specify an uncontrolled factor that could affect the comparison.
rubric: Identify all three planned spatial changes.
Distinguish target timing from measured timing.
Keep intention, event and interpretation separate.
